subject: Business Models
title: Surge Pricing Ethics
description: A 60-second lesson on Surge Pricing Ethics.

hook.text: During Hurricane Sandy, Uber prices surged 8x. A $20 ride cost $160. Public outrage erupted.

buildup.text: Surge pricing uses supply-demand economics: high demand and low supply drives prices up automatically.

discovery.text: Economists defend surge pricing: higher prices attract more drivers, actually increasing supply during crises.

twist.text: The public sees it as price gouging. Uber caps surge at 2x during natural disasters now.

climax.text: The tension between economic efficiency and public perception defines dynamic pricing's future.

punchline.text: 8x during a hurricane. Efficient or exploitative? The debate rages.

quiz.question: How does Uber now handle surge pricing during natural disasters?

details.summary: Surge pricing increases marketplace prices during high demand periods to balance supply and demand. While economically rational because it incentivizes more supply to come online, surge pricing during emergencies, weather events.
details.whyItMatters: Surge pricing is the most visible example of marketplace algorithm ethics. The tension between efficient price signaling and exploitation during vulnerable moments forces marketplaces to balance profit maximization with social responsibility and.
takeaways: Higher prices during peak demand incentivize additional supply to come online
Surge pricing during emergencies triggers public outrage and regulatory scrutiny
Marketplaces impose caps and ethical guidelines to manage surge pricing backlash

faq.question: Is surge pricing ethically justified from an economic standpoint?
faq.answer: Economically, higher prices signal scarcity and incentivize supply. During a storm, surge pricing motivates more drivers to work. Without it, nobody gets a ride. But when basic needs are affected, pure market pricing feels exploitative..

faq.question: How do marketplaces manage the ethics of surge pricing?
faq.answer: Uber caps surge multipliers during natural disasters. Some platforms disable surge during declared emergencies. Transparency about why prices are higher reduces backlash. Donated surge revenue during crises improves perception. Anti-price-gouging laws in many jurisdictions set legal limits.
